Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

candidates.explanation: Coordinated pipeline-aware relaxation: when recent demand exceeds baseline, reduce orders at all nodes to prevent upstream backlog while maintaining pipeline flow. Node0 reduces more to avoid over-ordering, node1 and node2 reduce moderately to keep pipeline steady.

Downstream service protection: increase orders at upstream nodes when downstream backlog is high, but only if pipeline is not excessive. Node0 and node1 increase to replenish, node2 increases to support node1.
Balanced response: if growth is high and backlog exists, increase orders slightly to meet demand, but cap to avoid overshoot. If pipeline is already high, reduce to prevent upstream backlog.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.

Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. candidates.explanation: This rule set aims to mitigate the emergency by increasing orders at all nodes when recent demand exceeds baseline, while also considering backlog and pipeline to avoid over-ordering. The first rule boosts orders at node 0 when growth is high and backlog exists. The second rule increases orders at node 1 when its backlog is high, ensuring it can meet downstream demand. The third rule increases orders at node 2 when its backlog is high, to replenish upstream supply. The fourth rule provides a small boost when growth is high but backlog is low, to proactively build inventory.

This rule set focuses on pipeline-aware adjustments. It increases orders when pipeline is low relative to recent demand, and reduces orders when pipeline is high to prevent overstock. The first rule boosts node 0 orders if pipeline is less than recent demand and backlog exists. The second rule boosts node 1 orders if pipeline is less than recent demand and backlog exists. The third rule boosts node 2 orders if pipeline is less than recent demand and backlog exists. The fourth rule reduces orders at any node if pipeline is very high relative to recent demand, to avoid excess inventory.

This rule set uses a combination of growth and backlog to scale orders. It increases orders proportionally to backlog when growth is high, and also adds a base increase when growth is high regardless of backlog. The first rule applies to all nodes: if growth>1.5 and backlog>0, increase by min(6, backlog*0.3). The second rule adds a fixed increase of 2 when growth>1.5. The third rule reduces orders if inventory is very high and backlog is zero, to avoid overstock. The fourth rule provides a small increase when growth is moderately high (1.2-1.5) and backlog exists.

Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.

Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation: when inventory is high relative to backlog and pipeline, reduce orders to avoid excess inventory; when backlog exists, increase orders to recover service. Coordinated across nodes.
Demand-responsive: increase orders when recent demand exceeds baseline (growth > 1) to build pipeline, but cap increases to avoid overreaction. Decrease when growth < 1 and inventory is ample.
Backlog-first service: prioritize clearing backlog at all nodes by ordering up to backlog plus a safety stock, while limiting increases when inventory is already high.

candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation with coordinated backlog service: when backlog exists, order enough to cover backlog plus a safety margin, but reduce if inventory is already high. When no backlog and inventory is low, increase orders modestly to rebuild pipeline. When inventory is high and pipeline is sufficient, reduce orders to avoid excess inventory. This balances cost and downstream service without overreacting to uncertain demand.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.

Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.

Coordinated upstream support: node 2 increases order when downstream nodes have backlog or low inventory, while node 0 and 1 reduce orders if their pipeline is excessive. This aims to prevent starvation and reduce total cost.
Demand-growth responsive: if recent demand exceeds baseline (growth > 1.1), increase orders modestly to build pipeline; if pipeline is already high, reduce. Also reduce if inventory is excessive.
